Tluukt (F28)

Region (English scoring-table region): Bulwar.

In a sentence: A gnoll matriarch skilled in magic and betrayal contests for mastery of the valleys on Bulwar’s southern edge, turning fear into an empire.

v2.1 personality coordinates: Expansionism 97/100 | Authoritarianism 96/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 99/100 (100 = Magic, 0 = Artifice; theme intensity 88/100) | Pluralism 8/100. v2.1 values: Evil (6/100), with a stable trajectory. The missions explicitly enslave and sell Bulwari inhabitants and harpies, replenish the workforce after enslaved miners die, and treat subjects’ free will as something that may be taken away. Governance yields some public benefit through infrastructure, but its core treats sapient beings as resources.

Narrative: High | Mission-tree length: Very long (84 missions directly defined for F28, including conditional branches) | Verified version: Local Mod supports EU4 v1.37.5.0 | Uniqueness: Very high | Potential for a punishing campaign: High (leader’s life and death, early major wars, and subjects) | Early pressure: Very high | Expansion capacity: Very high.

Where the cleaver comes from

Tluukt is a 1444 starting country in the Šad Sur, belonging to the Sandfang Gnolls and following Xhazobkult. The local history file records the matriarch Tluukt as having taken power in 1413, describes her as cruel and scheming, and gives her very high Evocation magic ability. The offline English wiki gives a fuller account of her rise: Šad Sur had several warring gnoll packs that raided one another; Tluukt first built strength in the mountains, then expanded through raids on Bulwar’s fringe and sieges of old strongholds. This setting history does not mean the missions force the player to reenact every campaign. Source discrepancy: the retrieved wiki account places the beginning of Tluukt’s aggressive rise later than the local history file’s accession record; these accounts do not establish a reconciled chronology. The specific Wiki dating is recorded in the English source-check metadata.

Her aims go far beyond surviving the opening. Bulwar’s elven kingdoms, its Sun faith, human cities, and another powerful gnoll, Zokka, all stand between her and the Suran Valley. The mission tree branches around the conflict between Zokka and Jaddar: alliance, exploitation, betrayal, and annexation are not one mandatory sequence. The Chinese source’s research summary reports an offline-wiki setting chronology in which a Bulwari rebellion defeated Tluukt in 1452 and Jaddar’s legions eventually annexed her in later history; it explicitly distinguishes that narrative from a player’s inevitable in-game outcome. Source discrepancy: the retrieved English wiki’s “Rebellion and Decline” section says that after the major defeat Tluukt retreated to Ekyrigrax and lost the Suran Plain, but retained her gnollish subordinates and the Šad Sur; it does not support the later-annexation claim. Its account of posthumous assimilation concerns the remnants of Zokka’s pack. The Chinese-source summary and retrieved English passage are retained as separate claims; no independent historical reassessment is made here.

The wiki also portrays her as a politician unlike an ordinary bandit chief: early on, she refused tribute to the packs controlling old fortresses, destroyed her opponents through mountain ambushes and prolonged sieges, and exploited the exhaustion of Bulwar’s kingdoms in the decade beginning in 1430 to seize land. Her cruelty is not aimless frenzy; it is how she builds prestige and buys the loyalty of her followers. Her enemies see a marauder; her followers see a leader finally capable of overcoming the old elven order. Both perspectives help explain why the missions combine magical duels with statecraft.

What must be done while she lives

The tree’s defining feature is its leader time limit. While Tluukt herself lives, magic and mission rewards strongly shape the early pace; after her death, how the country remembers her depends on what she accomplished in life. The campaign sends you toward Suran while also asking you to manage mountain packs, ports, slave mines, subjects, and a tribute network. This is not simply a matter of sweeping across the map: the goal is to turn packs that survive by raiding into a ruling structure able to govern land, mobilize artisans, and organize armies. Later, several subject-pack and vassal paths make the campaign feel more like managing a dangerous web of influence.

Opening decisions depend heavily on circumstances. If Zokka stabilizes the east, Tluukt faces a powerful but untrustworthy kinsman as an ally; if Jaddar gains the upper hand, she must seize the valley before the elven legions advance. The tree’s hidden and conditional branches serve these different situations, so “betray Zokka” is not the one correct strategy. The player should instead treat the matriarch’s magical advantage as a way to buy time: her legacy will endure, but she cannot manage the subject network forever on behalf of her successors.

This “governance” does not erase the abuses. Current mission text plainly describes enslaved miners dying in large numbers and being replaced, profits made by enslaving harpies, and Bulwari inhabitants being made to obey the packs as either free subjects or slaves. Tluukt is not merely a conventional warmonger: she treats people as expendable resources and fear as an instrument of order. The values assessment is therefore Evil, based on enslavement and the denial of personhood—not on gnoll identity, warfare, or Xhazobkult itself.

The mission tree’s “new age of monsters” is a conditional future: if gnolls defeat elven hegemony and remake Bulwar, they may become regional overlords rather than frontier raiders. This is not the same as the later decline recorded by the wiki, nor should missions for other gnoll formables in older material be automatically counted among F28’s 84 missions. The campaign suits players who enjoy a powerful-mage opening, time pressure, intrigue and diplomacy, subject management, and a dark imperial narrative; it is a poor fit for those seeking a relaxed start or wishing to avoid enslavement themes. Some community players describe the opening as an exciting race against the matriarch’s lifespan, while others find the conditional branches and late-game subjects difficult to navigate. Versions and play setups differ, so treat these as experience notes only.

If looking for a “classic villain” for the personality test, Tluukt fits not because she looks monstrous, but because the missions show power organizing the economy, law, and enslavement at once—using political skill to systematically strip others of personhood.

National ideas (reference appendix)

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and scripted effects. Traditions apply when this idea set is adopted; its seven ideas unlock in sequence as idea slots are filled; the ambition applies after all seven are unlocked. Only national ideas are listed: racial, government, and mission rewards are not folded into these values. New ideas acquired through formation do not automatically stack with the old set. Idea descriptions may recount history or depict an intended future; they do not automatically describe events that have already occurred by 1444.

Tluukt (F28) — Tluukt Ideas

Traditions: Tluukt Traditions

Effects: National supply limit modifier: +25%; subject tribute income: +20%.

Idea 1: Honouring the Old

Gnolls share a long history with Bulwar. In 984 BA gnolls have invaded Bulwar for the first time, establishing several kingdoms there with the greatest of all being the All-High Kingdom of Zehia, centered around Sur mountains. Zehia's core land occupied roughly the same territory Tluukt holds in 1444, and many of our gnolls are direct descendants of the first invaders. The gnollish rule over Bulwar continued to wax and wane through centuries, until eventually being ended by the elves under Jaher. Defeated by Jaherian legions, gnolls ended up pushed into the hills and deserts on the outskirts of Bulwar with almost no city centres under direct control.

And yet, we remain and remember. We remember the glory of the past, we remember the successes of the Xhazobines, we remember the Age of Monsters. We do remember it all... but Bulwari humans seem to be forgetting, and the time has come for gnolls to remind them.

Effects: Foreign Core Duration: -10%; horde unity: +1; legitimacy: +1; devotion: +1; republican tradition: +0.3.

Idea 2: Cleaving the New

Tluukt is a conglomeration of several disparate tribes of southern Bulwar, united in early 1400s by Tluukt, a powerful gnollish mage. Tluukt is saddened by the state in which gnolls of Bulwar are found today and she believes that the gnollish society should be reformed.

She wishes to restore the gnollish rule to Bulwar by modernising the structure of gnollish packs and ensuring both internal stability and total loyalty and support of subjects. Having already done so inside her pack, Tluukt now looks north towards Bulwar proper. The Cleaver of Realms shall make a new grand gnollish state, and none may stand in her way.

Effect: Core-Creation Cost: -10%.

Idea 3: Denying the Sun Its Glory

The fall of Zokka came to Tluukt as a shock at first. A powerful ally, he was slain in a single combat with the pack utterly collapsing. But then, Tluukt saw an opportunity. Thousands of gnollish soldiers willingly joined our pack, filled with zealous rage and fury against Jaddar and his elven kind. The Devourer of the Sun might have fell, but the sun has not seen the last of gnolls just yet.

Effect: Land morale: +10%.

Idea 4: Indirect Gnollish Rule

Our human subjects tend to get scared easily by our gnollish nature. While we are not directly opposed to it - it is nice knowing they fear their rulers - this eventually can get very tiresome and annoying, especially when trying to deal with them.

Luckily, not all humans are like that and there are those that are able to listen to orders and execute them. Using them as our intermediates we can hold an indirect control over humans. Tight enough to hold them under control, loose enough to let them do their work.

Effect: Liberty Desire in Same Continent Subjects: +1500%.

Idea 5: Hidden Caches

While gnolls are primarily known as scavengers, we are also good at hiding supplies that might be needed later. When Jaher and his legions invaded Bulwar and ended gnollish rule, countless of hidden weapons, maps and pieces of armour were lost in the sands. Luckily for us, neither humans not elves were able to find those caches, allowing Tluukt armies to finally utilise them centuries later.

Effect: Army attrition: -10%.

Idea 6: Reignited Bulwari Slavery

Slavery is a large part of gnollish society, and our loss of control over Bulwar severely limited and practically ended the practice of slavery in the region. This changed when our Pack Mistress has managed to enfold the humans' into the pack's domain following invasion of Bulwar proper, bringing a large amount of potential slaves to the market. Citizens of humans were left in shock after our slavemasters started rounding up random humans, putting them in chains and sending south to Tluukt's palace. Let Bulwari slavery be reignited in defiance of wannabe gods and their blind followers!

Effect: Goods produced modifier: +10%.

Idea 7: Last Stand In Ekluzagnu

Following the death of its founder, Tluukt faced defeat after defeat against elves and Bulwari humans alike, until eventually the gnolls were surrounded in Grixekyr. The pack continued to exist in such a state for the next few decades, continually fortifying their lands and deterring increasingly rare Bulwari attacks. Alas, all good things must come to an end.

In 1507 Tluukt's old enemies, the Jaddari, declared the final war against the gnolls in Bulwar. While some traitorous gnolls sided with the elves and accepted the Jadd, the loyal gnolls of Tluukt fought to the last soldier, but despite their ferocity were pushed back all the way into the recently restored Ekluzagnu. Here, the Jaddari led an extremely long and costly siege, fighting floor by floor to kill every single gnoll in the fortress. Ironically, the very same place destroyed by Xhazobine ended up being the site of last stand of gnollish rule in Bulwar.

Effect: Fort defense: +20%.

Ambition: Tluukt Ambition

Effect: Diplomatic reputation: +100%.
